messages:
Alex W: quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-swap I see a 12-18% regression on 8k seq FlashAttention runs when batching hits ~24 reqs. profiler shows heavy L2 -> SMEM stalls.
Maria K: ugh. which variant did you land? flashattn-v2-tiled or the paged-attn fallback?
Alex W: landed tiled-pipeline -> default route for medium-long sequences. We also changed the KV prefetch window (paged-kv) to prefetch 2 pages instead of 1. Perf logs:
```
[run id=2026-03-12T22:10] model: llama-13b, seq=8192, batch=24
tokens/s: 48k (expected ~57k)
SMEM throughput: 84GB/s (cap ~150GB/s)
stall: smem_bank_conflict ++, l2_read_wait
```
Cheng L: can you paste the occupancy and grid/block config? sounds like block-level tiling increased register pressure and lowered occupancy.
Alex W: sure — current kernel launch params (from debug dump):
```
blockDim.x=256, blockDim.y=1
warps_per_block=8
shared_mem=48KB
regs_per_thread=64
occupancy_est=0.35
``` 
Sara N: 0.35 occupancy is low. We probably hit the tradeoff where larger tile_x reduced global mem traffic but killed occupancy and forced more SMEM reuse, causing bank conflicts. Did the patch change pipeline stages (# of async copies)?
Alex W: yes — we added a 2-stage async pipeline for prefetch+compute to overlap memory. The intention was to hide L2 -> DRAM, but seems SMEM becomes the choke.
Maria K: can we try decreasing shared_mem usage by tiling height down (tile_h--) so regs_per_thread goes down? maybe switch to 1-stage pipeline for long seqs.
Cheng L: also check the KV cache layout: paged-kv puts pages contiguously but our prefetch stride might be causing bank aliasing. Try flipping page stride (page_stride = page_size * 1 vs *2) and re-run.
Alex W: running quick micro-bench now with two variants: (A) tile_x=64, 1-stage pipeline, prefetch=1 page; (B) tile_x=128, 2-stage pipeline, prefetch=2 pages (current). Results incoming.
perf-bot: Test queued: 1769951110-A (tile_x=64,1-stage,prefetch=1) — ETA ~12m
Alex W: quick flame output from A (12m): tokens/s: 59k, SMEM throughput: 98GB/s, occupancy_est=0.63. Bank-conflict errs down.
Maria K: nice, looks like occupancy is main issue.
Cheng L: for completeness, run with fused-attn (register-optimized) vs flashattn tiled, and also try quantized kernels if available — they often shift pressure from SMEM to registers.
Alex W: queued fused-attn-run and quantized-run. Also instrumented shared mem bank access pattern; here's a short snippet of problematic indexing:
```
// inner loop
int sm_idx = (thread_id * tile_w + lane) & SMEM_MASK;
// & mask interacts poorly with page_stride when page_stride%bank_count==0
```
Sara N: aha. mask-based wrap can alias banks for specific strides. Replace mask with modulo or adjust page_stride to be co-prime with bank_count.
Alex W: good call. I'll try page_stride+=1 (make it odd) and re-run variant A.
perf-bot: Test update: 1769951110-B (page_stride adjusted) — queued — ETA ~8m
Alex W: new run with page_stride odd: tokens/s 60.2k, SMEM throughput 102GB/s, no bank conflict warnings. This matches expected gains.
Maria K: solid. Action items: 1) revert default to tile_x=64 for long sequences (can be heuristic by seq_len>6k & batch>16), 2) add page_stride coprime check in paged-kv prefetcher, 3) add occupancy failback to 1-stage pipeline when occupancy<0.5.
Cheng L: add a metric in console to flag SMEM bank_conflict ratio per model/route, so we can detect regressions earlier.
Alex W: will open PR with heuristic + tests. also adding microbench into CI so we don't regress again. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Sara N: nice triage. follow-up: can we add an automated sweep job to find good (tile_x, pipeline_stages, prefetch) combos per GPU type? keep it small first.
Alex W: yes — starting with A100 and H100 sweeps. will post results in this thread when ready.
